---
title: "Return results"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(mcplite)
```

Start with ordinary R return values. Use `tool_result()` when a client needs
structured data, rich content, result metadata, or an explicit tool-level
error. This guide builds on [Write tools](writing-tools.html); the examples run
without starting a server.

## Return an ordinary value

A tool can return a calculation, a string, or a named list directly:

```{r ordinary-value}
inventory_value <- list(item = "coffee", count = 0L)
inventory_value
```

For a tool return, character values become literal text; character vectors are
joined with newlines. Other JSON-serializable values, such as this list, become
JSON in a text content block. Bare lists are ordinary values, not MCP result
objects. Returning a JSON-looking string does not opt into structured content.

See [Return-value mappings](../reference/mcplite-results.html) for exact empty,
missing, scalar, and array mappings. The distinction matters if a client or
output schema expects a particular JSON shape.

## Add structured data

Return `tool_result(structured_content = value)` when a client should receive
machine-readable data as well as text:

```{r structured-result}
result <- tool_result(
  structured_content = list(item = "coffee", count = 0L),
  meta = list(source = "local inventory")
)
result$content[[1]]$text
```

When you omit `content`, `tool_result()` generates one JSON text fallback
block. If you supply content explicitly, it is kept without an extra fallback:

```{r explicit-content, results = "hide"}
tool_result(
  content = content_text("Coffee is out of stock."),
  structured_content = list(item = "coffee", count = 0L)
)
```

Choose text that remains useful on its own: older protocols can omit structured
content or restrict its shape. The [compatibility table](../reference/mcp_server.html#protocol-compatibility)
shows what each supported version receives. JSON-looking strings, including
jsonlite `json` objects, remain string values in structured content; they are
not parsed or inserted as raw JSON.

## Include rich content

Build an ordered list of `content_*()` blocks. For example, return a short
summary with a self-contained text resource:

```{r content-blocks, results = "hide"}
tool_result(content = list(
  content_text("Inventory snapshot attached."),
  content_resource(
    uri = "inventory:snapshot",
    text = "item,count\ncoffee,0\ntea,5\n",
    mime_type = "text/csv"
  )
))
```

The [content constructors](../reference/content-blocks.html) also support
images, audio, and resource links, with optional annotations and metadata.
Image, audio, and resource blob payloads must already be base64-encoded: the
constructors do not read files, download URLs, infer MIME types, or encode the
data. Tool authors own payload integrity, access checks, and size limits.

A resource link carries your URI; it does not add a resource endpoint or make
the URI readable through the server. Audio, resource links, and per-content
metadata require MCP `2025-06-18` or later. A `2024-11-05` call returning audio
or a resource link receives a contained tool-level error, not partial content.

For expected failures, set `is_error = TRUE` as shown in
[Report failures](writing-tools.html#report-failures).

## Advertise structured output

Use `output_schema` on the tool to describe its structured result. This example
returns an array of strings:

```{r output-schema}
search_items <- tool(
  function(query) {
    matches <- paste(query, c("alpha", "beta"), sep = "-")
    tool_result(structured_content = matches)
  },
  name = "search_items",
  description = "Find local items whose names start with a query.",
  arguments = list(query = type_string()),
  output_schema = type_array(type_string())
)
search_items("tea")$structured_content
```

The schema is descriptive: `mcplite` checks container shape and
serializability, not full schema validity or result conformance. The tool owns
those guarantees. Modern MCP `2026-07-28` clients can receive this array schema
and structured value; legacy clients cannot. The tool remains available and
the generated text fallback still represents the matches. See the
[compatibility table](../reference/mcp_server.html#protocol-compatibility)
for object-shaped results and other versions.

## Choose payload encoding at startup

If default JSON mappings do not fit your payload, set package-global options
near the top of the server script, before constructing results and calling
`mcp_server()`. Keep them stable while the server runs. The
[results reference](../reference/mcplite-results.html#payload-json-options)
lists the defaults, supported choices, and an executable example.

These options affect payload values, not protocol fields, schemas, annotations,
or result and content metadata. The tool still owns output-schema conformance.
For a per-tool text representation, return your own JSON as ordinary character
text, for example `as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(value, na = "null"))`; it stays
literal text rather than becoming structured content.
